newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IBIS DAX higher pre-bourse, 3,800 in sight.
newsitem.headline: German IBIS DAX higher pre-bourse, 3,800 in sight.

text.p: German shares traded strongly ahead in pre-bourse electronic trade on Monday, with the IBIS DAX index lifted by a nearly one-percent rise on Wall Street on Friday and the continued support of a firm dollar.
By 0752 GMT the IBIS DAX index was up 15.13 points, or 0,40 percent, at 3,767.50 points, while the June DAX futures contract, which expires this week, was up 22 points at 3,771.

"Basically there isn't a whole lot around to talk about this morning. We're higher on the back of Wall Street and we could reach 3,800 points during bourse trade. Turnover is very thin," a Frankfurt broker said.
The Dow Jones Industrial index ended trade on Friday up 70.57 points at 7,782.04 points, a rise of nearly one percent, after another rampant week in Wall Street's greatest bull-run in history.
The Dow Jones industrial average has gained 1,000 points in just a little over a month after portfolio managers have ploughed fresh cash into stocks.

The rise on Friday came after a larger-than-expected drop in May wholesale prices. Analysts in the U.S. are expecting Tuesday's release of May consumer prices to further reinforce optimism in the U.S.
This is expected to feed further gains for the German stock market, which has been following the U.S. index slavishly in recent weeks.
The strong dollar helped lift chemical stocks, including Degussa, up 1.11 marks at 94.90 marks. Bayer was up 44 pfennigs at 67.80 marks, while Merck KGaA was up 90 pfennigs at 74.70 marks.
